extracted.intended_audience: students of literature / readers of Schlegel's lectures (literary students and critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for judging and producing literary works (poetry, criticism, national literature) as articulated in Schlegel's lectures and accompanying questions. Focuses on judgement, language, originality, national character, and the balance of imagination and reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false taste and affectation; reject narrow imitation of the antique
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘avoid false taste and affectation in our art and poetry. The imitation of the antique ... is conducted on narrow principles.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: slavish copying of classical/antique models or mannerisms that create affectation rather than genuine poetic quality. Guidance: be selective when borrowing from the past; do not adopt antique forms or 'the best part' of predecessors uncritically. Aim for genuine expression rather than imitation for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise judgement and perfecting existing work over ostentatious invention
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘We should be ambitious to perfect what has been begun, not to shew our invention at the expense of our judgment.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring note: value sustained improvement, coherence, and considered judgment above flashy novelty. Anti-pattern: inventiveness that undermines coherence, taste, or critical soundness; works that show originality but lack disciplined judgment should be downgraded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine imagination and reason with steadiness of will and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: To the 'profoundness of reason' and 'fulness and majesty of fancy' there must be added 'that stableness of will and purpose, which brings the seeds of good to maturity, and guards them from the first encroachments of corruption.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should reward works where energetic imagination and philosophical depth are matched by consistent artistic will and long-term purpose (discipline, editorial restraint). Anti-pattern: brilliant but erratic or ephemeral works lacking follow-through or integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlightened judgment: clarity, universality of observation, and moral discernment
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The clearness of an enlightened judgment must watch over those mighty energies of reason and of fancy. True judgment depends in all things upon universality of observation, and discernment of that which is right, in the midst of much more that is wrong.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for quality: assess whether the author demonstrates broad observation (wide reading/experience), clear critical thought, and the ability to distinguish what is valuable in a work amid defects. Examples: works that show discriminating taste and wide reference score higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rhetorical arts that please ears but do not aid judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The author states an aim 'to discriminate between the good and the evil, without any ambition to display those arts of rhetoric which might have pleased your ears, but could not have aided your judgment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: ornate rhetorical flourishes that obscure substance. Reward plainness or restraint where it clarifies argument or aesthetic judgement. Scoring guidance: form should serve critical clarity rather than mere ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and intellectual independence (self-derived thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fichte is praised because 'he takes the materials of thoughts entirely from himself, trusts every thing to nature, and depends in nothing upon those who have gone before him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive criterion: value originality and intellectual independence—works that generate ideas from the author's own imagination/experience rather than relying heavily on predecessors. Caveat: originality must still be guided by judgment and universality of observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of craft: depth, observation, wonder and mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Tieck is admired as 'a poet who is so perfectly master of all the depths, and observations, and wonders, and mysteries, of his art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical mastery (command of poetic devices, depth of imaginative vision, detailed observation, capacity to evoke wonder/mystery). Examples: sustained tonal control, rich imagery, and insightful detail are rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: National literature requires language, traditions, and history
rubrics_metrics.description: The lectures argue that besides poetry, 'national traditions and history' and the 'importance of language as a bond of union' are necessary to the formation of national literature; national poetry gives character and interest to a nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing works as contributions to national literature, consider fidelity to or engagement with national language, historical memory, and traditions. Works that enrich or reflect national character (through language, themes, historical consciousness) are positively scored. Anti-pattern: literature wholly alienated from national linguistic/traditional roots when judged in a national-literature context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language as the instrument of thought and essential to literary value
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated emphasis: 'language identical with thought', 'importance of language as a bond of union', and the claim that reason cannot act without language as an instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: clarity, precision, and force of expression are central; evaluate the suitability of diction, rhetorical structure, and how language shapes thought in the work. Anti-pattern: muddled expression or linguistic deficiency that weakens conceptual or aesthetic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate philosophical stance: empiricism for practical life, idealism for art
rubrics_metrics.description: The text notes empiricism 'has with justice become the ruling system in all that regards practical life, physics, and pure science' while 'idealism ... has exerted a powerful and an abiding influence upon our art, our criticism, and our higher philosophy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work aligns its philosophical approach appropriately to its aims: empirical/rational methods suit practical/scientific subjects, whereas idealist/idealizing modes may be more fitting for art and criticism. Penalise mismatches (e.g., overly abstract idealism in a work aiming at empirical social description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sectarianism and scholastic forms in criticism and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'spirit of sectarianism' and scholastic forms have declined and are described as producing imposing but erroneous systems; the spirit of sect has become milder and scholastic forms have sunk into contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: dogmatic, sectarian adherence to a single school or scholastic jargon that prevents honest critique or plural engagement. Prefer open, integrative criticism that avoids doctrinaire closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the mutual influence of public/readers and authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertion that 'literature will soon become much less the concern of individuals than of the public, and the influence of readers upon authors will at least be as that of authors upon readers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing literary work, consider audience influence and reception context: works that engage public sensibility responsibly or reflect meaningful dialogue between readers and authors are significant. Anti-pattern: hermetic works wholly ignoring readership when public engagement is the aim.
